children: Soybeans fell more than 1% to a two-month low on Monday, weighed down by supplies from a record US harvest entering the market and lower crude oil prices.
Corn and wheat prices also fell, though losses in wheat were limited by continued disruption to Black Sea supplies.
"We are seeing seasonal pressure on soybeans as US harvest is gathering pace," said one Singapore-based trader. "There are not many supportive factors for prices."
The most-active soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
lost 1.2% at $12.41-1/4 a bushel, as of 0338 GMT, having hit its weakest level since August 26 earlier in the session.
gave up 1.1% to $4.51 a bushel and wheat
Oil prices fell after surging to near six-month highs late last week, although ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus.

Last week, soybean prices were underpinned by strong export demand and higher crude oil prices. Crude oil often provides direction to agricultural markets because of the growing use of grains and oilseeds in making biofuels.

The US Department of Agriculture on Thursday reported net export sales of US soybeans in the week ended October 15 at 2.8 million metric tons, near the top end of market estimates, as a run of Chinese purchases boosted volumes.
Corn prices have been pressured by the advancing US harvest, which could further bolster large stocks.
The wheat market registered liquidation by investment funds last week as a round of US-led diplomacy aimed at ending Russia's war with Ukraine raised hopes of a revival of Black Sea grain trade.
But attacks have continued since the talks, including a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off the Romanian Black Sea coast.
